# Overview


## Setup 

```{r 'setup-multifactor', message = FALSE}
library(multifactor)

# Wrangling
library(dplyr)

# Plotting
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(systemfonts)
library(ragg)

# Load demo data
set.seed(2612)
fox <- quickbrownfox()

# Define utility function
split_to_letters <- function(x) unique(
  unlist(
    strsplit(gsub(" ", "", x), split = ""),
    recursive = TRUE, use.names = FALSE
  )
)
```

### Example Dataset: The Quick Brown Fox 


```{r 'prep-plots', echo = FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, dev='ragg_png'}
word_lvs <- c("the", "quick", "brown", "fox", "jumps", "over", "lazy", "dog")
cons_lvs <- c("subject", "predicate", "object")

letter2word_df <- as.data.frame(fox$letter2word) %>%
  mutate(
    word = factor(word, levels = word_lvs),
    label = "X"
  ) %>%
  arrange(word)

word2constituent_df <- as.data.frame(fox$word2constituent) %>%
  mutate(
    word = factor(word, levels = word_lvs),
    constituent = factor(constituent, levels = cons_lvs),
    label = "X"
  ) %>%
  arrange(constituent, word)


lm1 <- ggplot(letter2word_df) +
  geom_text(label = "X", x = I(0.5), y = I(0.5)) +
  ggtitle("Words to letters") +
  facet_grid(word ~ letter, switch = "y", space = "free_x")


lm2 <- ggplot(word2constituent_df) +
  geom_text(label = "X", x = I(0.5), y = I(0.5)) +
  ggtitle("Words to Constituents") +
  facet_grid(word ~ constituent, switch = "y", space = "free_x")

d <- "
AAAAAA
BBCCCC"

lm1 + lm2 + plot_spacer() +
  plot_layout(
    axes = "collect", axis_titles = "collect",
    nrow = 2L, design = d
  ) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme_bw() &
  theme(
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.1, "lines")
  )
```

```{r 'show-data', message = FALSE}
levels(fox)

as.matrix(fox$letter2word)
```

### Calculate coverage
We'll need to generate some collection of letters as input data. 
```{r 'setup-example1', message = FALSE}
input <- split_to_letters("some collection of letters")

input
```

We can use the `weave_coverage()` function to calculate to what degree the input
letters cover the words in our data set. This function behaves similarly to 
`weave()` but comes with an additional argument, `.data`. For now, let's plug in
our input letters: 
```{r 'weave-example1', message = FALSE}
res <- weave_coverage(
  x = fox, .path = letter ~ word, .data = input
)

res
```

Now, let's use a second set of letters that are explicitly part of the sentence: 
```{r 'setup-example2', message = FALSE}
input <- split_to_letters("jumps over")

input
```

```{r 'weave-example2', message = FALSE}
res <- weave_coverage(
  x = fox, .path = letter ~ word, .data = input
)

res
```
Notice that the column named `"complete"` marks two particular words as complete 
now. 

We can use the `subset()` method for `linkmap` to automatically filter for 
complete cases:
```{r 'weave-subset', message = FALSE}
subset(res)
```
